Hajduboszormeny Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Hajdúböszörmény, Hungary

Not demolished. An organized Jewish community existed in Hajdúböszörmény by the 1850s, with its burial society founded in 1846 on land donated by the village; the oldest grave (1848) belongs to Ezriel Katz. The Orthodox community split in 1890 after litigation between Rabbi Áron Fried and dissenting followers led some to form a separate Hasidic congregation. By January 1941, 934 Jews (about 3% of residents) lived there, mostly artisans and merchants involved in the grain trade, maintaining their own Orthodox elementary school. In 1942, local police ordered the community to report any refugees and refrain from helping them. Following Germany's March 1944 occupation, the district's deputy administrator ordered ghettos established that May; Mayor Antal Szalkay assigned the synagogue and surrounding area as the ghetto, with transition beginning May 27. In mid-June, all residents were confined at the local pig market, robbed by Hungarian gendarmes, and transferred to a brick factory in Debrecen before deportation between June 25-28 - some to Strasshof in Austria, others to Auschwitz. This cemetery remains active, with its last known burial in 2007.
